description: The BINARY family end to end: BINARY and VARBINARY columns declare and describe, a scripting variable can be DECLAREd or LET with either spelling and its value inserted, and a BEGIN...END block can RETURN one. BINARY text is BARE UPPERCASE HEX in both directions - a VARCHAR-to-BINARY cast reads the string as hex and non-hex text is refused, a BINARY value displays as bare hex, and TO_BINARY with UTF-8 round-trips through it. Snowflake's decoder knows NO 0x prefix and refuses one exactly as it refuses any other non-hex text - from a cast, from TO_BINARY and from HEX_DECODE_BINARY alike, in either letter case - while the TRY_ forms answer NULL instead of raising and the bare spelling still decodes. Frostlake used to strip the prefix, so those cases were once written in a spelling no account accepts. Converted from types/BinaryTypeTest, which keeps only its two type-model unit tests (see the task note); the Java's BinaryType.parseValue and formatValue checks are expressed here through LENGTH, TO_VARCHAR with UTF-8 and the value's own display form.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE binary_test (id INTEGER, data BINARY)
CREATE TABLE varbinary_test (id INTEGER, data VARBINARY)
SELECT CAST('48656C6C6F' AS BINARY) AS result

SELECT LENGTH('48656C6C6F'::BINARY) AS a, TO_VARCHAR('48656C6C6F'::BINARY, 'UTF-8') AS b
